heating_rate_per_second.note: Not derived from experimental data. With pan=150C and duration=240s this predicts approximately 138C. Domain warnings are expected. Replace after validation.

start_temperature_c.note: Represents approximate onset of visible coagulation. Egg white and yolk differ. This model treats them as uniform.

complete_temperature_c.note: Represents approximate completion of coagulation under simplified uniform model.

evaporation_rate_g_per_sec_per_celsius.note: Not derived from experimental data. Chosen to produce visible but not extreme water loss over 4 minutes at high temperature. Replace after validation against measured data.

pan_surface_weight.note: Weight given to pan temperature in effective_surface_temp blend. 0.30 means surface is approximately 70% food temperature plus 30% pan temperature. Not derived from heat-transfer theory.

base_rate_per_second.note: Browning rate at onset center temperature with no moisture suppression. Not fitted to experimental data.

q10_factor.note: Rate doubles per 10 degrees Celsius above onset center. Standard Q10 biological approximation. Not validated for Maillard reaction in eggs.

onset_center_c.note: Sigmoid center temperature where onset factor equals 0.50. Literature range 140 to 150 degrees Celsius for food surfaces.

onset_steepness.note: Controls sigmoid sharpness. Higher value means sharper onset transition. Not fitted to experimental data.

moisture_suppression_exponent.note: Controls how strongly water fraction suppresses browning rate. Not fitted to experimental data.

burn_rate_multiplier.note: Scales burn index progression beyond browning threshold. Not fitted to experimental data.

stickiness_protein_weight.note: Scales protein denaturation contribution to stickiness index. Not fitted to experimental data.

stickiness_temp_weight.note: Scales surface temperature contribution to stickiness index. Not fitted to experimental data.

butter_protection_exponent.note: Controls how effectively butter melt fraction reduces stickiness. Not fitted to experimental data.
